front.text: White left the e4 pawn and played 4.Bc4. What is this called, and what is White's idea?

cards.back: The Von Hennig Gambit. White gives up the e4 pawn and plays f3 next, to open the f-file and go after f7 together with the bishop on c4.

front.text: How do you meet the Von Hennig Gambit? Play your next 3 moves.

cards.back:
- 4...Nf6 develops and guards the pawn on e4.
- 5...exf3 just take it. If White takes back with the queen, [5...exf3 6.Qxf3 Qxd4] wins a second pawn and hits the bishop on c4.
- 6...Bf5 the Caro-Kann bishop comes out before ...e6 shuts it in.

front.text: White has castled. What are your next 2 moves?

cards.back:
- 7...e6 shuts the c4 bishop's diagonal to f7 and lets your own bishop out.
- 8...Bg6 guards f7 once more and takes the bishop off the open f-file. The same move answers [7...e6 8.Ng5 Bg6].
- Don't take on c2: after [8.Ne5 Bxc2 9.Nxf7 Bxd1 10.Nxd8 Kxd8 11.Rxd1] the queens are off, your king is stuck in the middle and e6 is weak.
- Next comes ...Bd6, ...Nbd7 and castling: you are a healthy pawn up.
